step_0_brainstorm_summary.core_tension_identified: FUNDAMENTAL TENSION: eShunt's primary function is to DRAIN CSF (with dissolved therapeutics) to the venous system. Chronic drug delivery INTO CSF lumen is rapidly cleared (~5 min half-life vs ~30 min for VP shunt). This tension does NOT affect ACUTE BOLUS delivery (drainage paused 1-4h) or SENSORS (sensor reads CSF; drainage removes sampled CSF but sensor stays). The most eShunt-compatible CNS therapy platform mechanism is therefore BIOSENSING rather than drug delivery.

step_6_first_attack.attack_name: Cognos US10786155B2 closest prior art attack
step_6_first_attack.strongest_alternative_identified: Cognos Therapeutics US10786155B2 — 'Skull-mounted drug and pressure sensor' (granted 2020-09-29). This is the closest prior art for M10 (CSF biosensor). Cognos has a patent FAMILY (US10786155B2, US11529443B2, US11883203B2, US20230191095A1) covering skull-mounted CSF drug+sensor+microdialysis combinations.
step_6_first_attack.attack_statement: Cognos US10786155B2 teaches an implantable skull-mounted drug+pressure+optical CSF sensor with Bluetooth wireless, LED bundle for optical absorption profiling of CSF, photodetector, drug delivery port, microcontroller subsystems, and pressure+temperature sensor. M10 is just an eShunt-specific application of Cognos's general concept. A PHOSITA would adapt Cognos's skull-mounted design to endovascular route. The skull-mounted vs endovascular distinction is mere anatomical application of the same sensing principle. The Cognos family broadly teaches CSF biomarker sensing + drug delivery + wireless communication, which §103 obviousness covers.
step_6_first_attack.defense_response: M10 SURVIVES ATTACK_1 CONDITIONALLY on 4 distinctions:
step_6_first_attack.defense_distinction_1_endovascular_vs_sk: Cognos requires cranial burr hole (open skull surgery under general anesthesia). M10 uses endovascular venous access (percutaneous jugular puncture under local anesthesia). Different surgical approach, different patient risk profile, different clinical workflow. NOT mere anatomical application — fundamentally different access modality. CereVasc's entire IP portfolio (US8672871B2, US9199067B2, US11850390B2, US11883309B2, US11951270B2, US12485256B2) is built on the endovascular access principle; this is CereVasc's core technical moat.
step_6_first_attack.defense_distinction_2_drainage_integrati: Cognos is standalone drug+sensor (no drainage function). M10 is INTEGRATED with eShunt CSF DRAINAGE function. The eShunt's primary clinical purpose is hydrocephalus/IIH drainage; adding biosensor is an EXTENSION of an existing drainage device. Cognos requires a separate standalone implant. Different device class, different clinical indication, different regulatory pathway.
step_6_first_attack.defense_distinction_3_flow_past_sensor_a: M10's flow-past-sensor architecture is unique to eShunt: CSF drainage flow (0.35 mL/min) continuously refreshes analyte at sensor surface. Cognos uses a STATIC CSF optical sensing chamber (no flow). This is a non-obvious engineering difference: eShunt drainage could be ADVANTAGEOUS (continuous fresh-CSF sampling without depletion) OR DISADVANTAGEOUS (flow affects sensor equilibrium). Cognos does not teach how to handle flow past sensor.
step_6_first_attack.defense_distinction_4_patient_population: M10 targets eShunt patient population (NPH/IIH with existing venous access for drainage). These patients ALREADY have an eShunt implanted for clinical drainage need; adding biosensor is a marginal enhancement. Cognos targets Alzheimer's/Parkinson's via standalone skull-mounted implant — different patient population, different clinical pathway.

negatives.candidate: M5 — Neuromodulation electrode via eShunt (DBS via venous access)
negatives.physics_reason: DBS targets (STN, GPi, VIM thalamus) are deep parenchymal structures 8-25mm below cortical surface. eShunt accesses SUBARACHNOID CSF space (between arachnoid and pia). Reaching deep nuclei from subarachnoid space requires parenchymal penetration, defeating the venous-access value proposition. Cortical surface stimulation (subdural electrodes) is a different therapy with different indications (epilepsy, not movement disorders).
negatives.prior_art_confirmation: SQ14 (Lens + Scopus) returned 21+6 hits on 'endovascular venous stimulation neural' — all confirm endovascular stent-electrodes exist (Synchron stentrode) but for CORTICAL surface recording via trans-arterial approach, NOT deep DBS targets via venous-sinus-to-subarachnoid route.

negatives.candidate: M8 — Chemotherapy for leptomeningeal metastases via eShunt
negatives.prior_art_evidence: Scopus SQ20 returned DIRECT HITS: 'Use of a stop-flow programmable shunt valve to maximize CNS chemotherapy delivery in a pediatric patient with acute lymphoblastic leukemia' (2014, Surgical Neurology International) + 'Programmable shunt valves with a virtual off for intrathecal chemotherapy delivery in children with high-grade CNS tumors and hydrocephalus' (2026, Child's Nervous System). The concept of pausing drainage for chemo delivery via shunt valve is established standard-of-care.
negatives.additional_physics_concern: Drainage pause is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with active hydrocephalus (high ICP at risk of herniation). Only safe for compensated patients with low ICP. Dual-lumen architecture needed for safe simultaneous drainage + chemo dwell — adds manufacturing complexity.
negatives.honest_concession: M8 was DIRECTLY DESTROYED by 2014 + 2026 prior art. Even if CereVasc's own US11850390B2 didn't exist, the stop-flow shunt valve for chemo delivery is established standard-of-care.

negatives.physics_concern: Drug released INTO CSF lumen is rapidly cleared by eShunt drainage (~5 min half-life vs ~30 min for VP shunt draining to peritoneum). three_questions_for_leading_candidate_M1.strongest_alternative: Cognos US10786155B2 skull-mounted drug+pressure+optical sensor. M10's eShunt-specific value over Cognos is endovascular access (no burr hole) + drainage integration (eShunt primary function) + flow-past-sensor architecture (unique to drainage device). Without these distinctions, M10 collapses into Cognos §103.
three_questions_for_leading_candidate_M1.what_failure_can_kill_us: Three failure modes: (1) §103 obviousness — if Cognos specification broadly teaches 'any biosensor modality' including endovascular variants, M10 is destroyed; (2) Sensor drift / biofouling over chronic 5+ year implant lifespan — CGM precedent suggests 20-year maturity timeline; (3) Multi-analyte identifiability — if biomarker signals are mathematically non-separable in CSF matrix (per #1 V24/V25 lesson), the multi-analyte value proposition collapses.
three_questions_for_leading_candidate_M1.why_worth_keeping: M10 fills a wide-open IP gap in CereVasc's portfolio (no biosensor patents) while leveraging CereVasc's existing endovascular access IP (US11850390B2 + US11883309B2). M10 turns the eShunt from a one-way drainage device into a two-way CNS interface (drainage + sensing) — a SYSTEM-LEVEL invention that no competitor has. Alzheimer's (50M patients), leptomeningeal disease (5-8% of cancer patients), and shunt infection (1-5% of shunt patients) all benefit from chronic CSF biomarker monitoring. M10 is the only candidate that addresses the eShunt's drainage-drug-delivery tension (sensors are unaffected by drainage).
